Thursday 5 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A

Lead one shared task per period for about ten pupils across BUILD, GROW and LAUNCH. Three TAs support hands-on. Theme: Plan the day out. The full-day visit is planned for a full day next term (date to be confirmed); no visit is booked by this pack.
Venue: the open-air museum. Owner handwritten venue name: ____________________. Add identifying details only to the private staff copy.
Set up before pupils arrive

Prepare three mixed home teams of 4, 3 and 3, adjusted for actual needs. Allocate P01–P10 privately; do not assign pathways or achievements in advance. Set A, B and C tables with job cards, P5 route sheets and research cards. Keep a quiet seated place. Set D with the accepted Lesson 6 resources, closed until P6. No cooking or new bake today.
Time
Teacher leads
TA support

Help each pupil find a role and first step
Five slides, one minute each
Read or point to the task and finish
P5 research and plan; model then circulate
One TA at each home team
Invite three short pitches or quiet shares
Keep each pupil’s own contribution
Stop, clear, regulate and preview P6
Count kit and swap paper packs
Model the budget; set the Lesson 6 goal
TA1 A, TA2 B, TA3 prepares D

Plan the day out continued
Thursday 5 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A
P5 say and show

“We are planning a full day at the open-air museum. Choose what you want to find out. Use a research card or an adult-approved extract. Mark what we know and what we still need to check. Finish one team plan: what to see, a then-and-now question, and who does what. You can pass on speaking, show your work or share quietly.”

13:00–13:03 teacher models one enquiry: “How did people wash clothes then? What does a tool or label show? What does a washing machine change now?” This is a research question, not a claim that the venue has that exhibit.

13:03–13:15 teams read, sort or discuss evidence and select one theme: Money then and now, Work and industry, or Home life. Use one compact route for the eventual visit, with different team questions. No separate walks are proposed. Keep a short route, warm seated rests and lunch needs on the owner check list.

13:15–13:20 complete a plan for a tabletop exhibit: one object sketch or permitted photo, a then-and-now caption with a source, and one unanswered question. Plan today; do not pretend to have visited. Assign navigator, recorder, photographer and kit lead. Two pupils may share one role. A pupil may combine manageable roles; an adult can help with the unfilled role.
13:20–13:25 invite one short team pitch. Ask consent before reading someone’s line. No cold calling. Retain who contributed what; a team plan or group photo does not establish everyone’s learning.
Reset from 13:25 to 13:35

Say “Stop, put tools down, keep your plan.” TAs count and park kit. Offer water, stretch or a quiet seated reset. Keep routes clear and pupils in the room. Swap to cost cards and calculators; there is no food or real cash. At 13:30 retain the reset across the period boundary. At 13:35 say “Now we check what the day might cost.”
Visible finish

P5 ends with one team plan and each pupil’s own contribution identified. P6 ends with one checked cost and a one-line team budget pitch. Routes are choices of help and demand; they are not pathway labels.
Plan the day out continued
Thursday 5 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A
P6 say and show

“These are practice allowances from our plan, not quotes. Cost ten pupils and four adults. Add entry, lunch and the optional shop reserve, then transport and contingency. Divide by ten pupil places to share all group costs. This is a planning allocation, not a charge to families. Buying nothing in the shop is valid.”

13:35–13:40 teacher models £150 pupil entry + £80 adult entry + £84 lunch/drink + £50 maximum shop reserve = £364 before transport. Show one addition, then leave a calculation for pupils. The £5 allowance is for each of ten pupils; adult shopping and personal extras are excluded.
Fourth station D uses existing Lesson 6

Teacher sets the goal: use real trial feedback to justify one change or confirmation. TA3 facilitates the accepted lesson id grow_community_cakesale_a2w1, held in GCS-2_SEGMENT_D, Lesson_06_A2_W1. Use its existing planner, task/evidence resources and staff guide; do not rebuild them. This owner order sets Thursday 5 November and overrides the older date printed in that source. This is a focused decision station, not delivery of the full 40-minute lesson.

TA1 stays with A; TA2 stays with B; the teacher leads from C and monitors the whole room. TA3 runs D at 13:40–13:48 and 13:49–13:57. Invite eligible GROW pupils in small groups while at least one pupil remains at each home team. Adjust the appointment list to actual membership. Return each pupil to complete their own cost check. Do not leave another team without support to create D.

At D use authentic trial records and an existing tool. Record the learner’s actual decision, reason and support against the existing Lesson 6 evidence id. If records are absent, mark the decision pending or practice; do not invent trial findings. Keep trip budgets separate from sale takings. No charitable funds are allocated to the trip.
Evidence and final close

14:00–14:10: teacher invites a point, sentence, drawing explanation or exact scribed line from each anonymous code. Link a permitted photo of the work or a work/observation reference; keep faces and identifiers out. If a photo is unsuitable, use a work reference and note why. Record actual support, absence or pending evidence honestly. One line per code indexes the fuller work; it does not complete an award.

Offer authentic explanation and response to the Communication portfolio. Use [AWARD] and [QUAL] as masks; staff check registered requirements privately. R follows an actual adult reply, NS and the learner’s own-colour or supported response. E records only actual banking. Keep the original work and approved storage route.

Owner checks before any commitment: venue opening and selected exhibits, short route and access, arrival/return times, meals, passenger/driver capacity, supervision, full return quote and omitted costs. Four adults is a model, not an approved staffing ratio. No enquiry, contact, payment, booking or publication is performed here.

paragraphs_in_document_order: Staff answers and cost checks
Thursday 5 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A
Use the practice allowances below. They preserve Proposal 1 amounts and update the model to ten pupils plus four adults. They are not venue prices or transport quotations.
Common item
Calculation
Amount
Pupil entry
Adult entry
Lunch and drink
Pupil shop reserve
10 × £5 maximum
Common subtotal
Practice option
Existing minibus
Hired minibus
Hired coach
Return transport
Before contingency
10% contingency
Planning total
Per pupil place ÷ 10

The per-pupil-place calculation allocates adult and shared costs across ten places; no family charge is implied. A per-traveller comparison divides by fourteen instead: £40.39, £63.96, £79.67, rounded to the nearest penny. Rounding each share may not reconstruct the exact group total. Keep the unrounded group total as the budget.
The 10% allowance applies to the full practice total, including the maximum shop reserve. It is a planning allowance, not a guaranteed ceiling. Actual additional costs may exceed it.
Staff answers and cost checks continued
Thursday 5 November 2026 | 12:50–14:10 | Year A
Shopping and full day costs

Buying nothing is valid. £5 less £3.20 leaves £1.80; £5 less £0 leaves £5. If every pupil chooses no purchase and the reserve is removed for a revised scenario, common cost is £314. With 10% contingency: existing minibus £510.40 (£51.04 per pupil place), hired minibus £840.40 (£84.04), coach £1,060.40 (£106.04). Do not treat a reserve as money actually spent.

The existing minibus allowance covers provisional fuel, parking and operating allocation. Hired allowances assume return transport, driver, waiting, parking and tax; an owner quote must confirm them. A hired driver is outside the four supervising adults. Their entry/lunch, if needed, is not costed. Staff driving cannot supervise while driving. Capacity, staffing, extra driver costs, access arrangements, cover and supplements remain unconfirmed. Do not pick the cheapest option before those checks.
P5 answers are evidence based choices

Accept different interests and questions. A sound plan names a wanted stop as unconfirmed, a useful question, a source or check needed, and workable shared jobs. An exhibit needs evidence for its caption. A modern price conversion or a claim about everyone in the past needs evidence; keep an unanswered question instead of guessing.
P6 pitch and common errors

Model: “Using the practice allowances, we recommend ___ if capacity and access are confirmed. Our planning total is £___, or £___ per pupil place, including lunch, the maximum shop reserve and 10% contingency.” A different choice can be justified. Spot: dividing shared costs only by team size; forgetting adults or return travel; treating £5 as compulsory spend; calling a practice allowance a quote.
Hinge and support

Privately ask or show: “Which divisor shares the whole cost over ten pupil places: 10 or 14?” Use 10 for that allocation; 14 is the separately labelled per-traveller average. If unclear, model one step then return the task. Prompt ladder: point, short question, rephrase, scaffold or choice, model first step only. Never cold call or require a public answer.

Existing Lesson 6 decisions stay with id grow_community_cakesale_a2w1. Keep its original evidence requirements and any unfinished work visible. The station and the Local Choice evidence line do not imply full lesson, unit or award completion.
